unmapped_findings: For the 17Al alloy, aging at 525 °C for 10 h gave the lowest-hardness aged condition of its series (616.8 ± 12.3 HV), consistent with the slow β-Mn precipitation kinetics at this low aging temperature; only 20.5 % β-Mn had formed with the α matrix largely untransformed (b0041, b0030, b0038).

The increase in Al content slowed the β-Mn precipitation kinetics during aging: whereas the 15Al α matrix almost completely transformed to β-Mn within 3 h at 525 °C, the 17Al and 19Al alloys required 6 h and 10 h, respectively, at 550 °C, so the 525 °C/10 h condition for 17Al remained only partially transformed (b0065, b0053).
